assumptions.text: Skalvion Electronics has a qualified accessory conversion cell that cuts and finishes supplied denim laminate. It does not weave denim. This capability is an added synthetic story assumption.
MAT000-7B remains the pre-cut jeans fabric component from the existing campaign fixture. One component is needed per jeans wristband; it is not the full smart band.
The fictional local material SKL-DENIM-PC-07 is assumed approved as equivalent to MAT000-7B. The mapping is supplied explicitly, not inferred from similar names or an implemented ontology service.
The frozen demo clock is 2026-10-01 09:00 America/Los_Angeles, matching smyle_campaign_demo.json. Observations end at that time. Future values are projections, never measured telemetry.

Week 1 preserves the existing fixture: 1,860 required units, 600 net on hand, 400 confirmed inbound, and 860 incremental units needed. These are future planning needs, not another count of prior-week orders.
Week 2 repeats 1,860 demand and adds a new 1,000 baseline supplier units. This second week, exact daily requirement profile, and inbound arrival dates are new synthetic assumptions.

Both accessory cells are staffed 08:00-16:00 every calendar day, including weekends, with a 12:00-13:00 break. Reserved order, maintenance and setup minutes are deducted before calculating new capacity. ACC-01 is fully committed and contributes no incremental capacity.

All four operations on ACC-02 have dedicated equipment and staff. Inspection constrains the route to a conservative 40 good components per net available hour. The rate includes normal speed and quality losses; do not multiply by OEE or 98% yield a second time.

Sixty square metres of approved denim laminate are uncommitted after existing jobs. Each started component consumes 0.018 square metres including normal cutting waste. A 98% planning yield determines gross starts and raw-material consumption.

Each proposed daily lot is quality released and packed by 16:00 and received at Morvanto at 08:00 the following calendar day. Daily requirements are due by the end of their date. Transfer capacity is assumed sufficient.
All Smyle recovery lots are proposed and unreleased. No Smyle production is present in observed history. Existing jobs produce a comparable accessory liner and remain reserved.

Other components, final assembly capacity and downstream logistics are assumed sufficient. The assessment proves material recovery over 14 days under these assumptions; it does not prove all future or Q4 demand can be met.
Custom vendor-neutral mock payloads are served from static files. No real Oracle, SAP, MES, BDC, Reltio or Dremio connection, data product, API compatibility, or trained predictive model is claimed.

get_shopfloor_snapshot.description: Plant, line, material, pipeline and current-state cards

get_shopfloor_timeseries.description: Return 16 daily aggregate rows by default. Use the 456 interval rows only for charts or a requested line/date range.

get_material_capacity.description: Daily capacity and material supply/demand projections, with decision summary

get_recovery_proposal.description: Read-only proposed production lots and approval handoff for Act 3

before_connection.description: Optional initial state before the mock skill or MCP is made available

integration_notes: Load the JSON locally and return the chosen response object.
Do not return the entire fixture if only a KPI or daily series is needed.
No HTTP endpoint, credentials, outbound request or production-order write is required.
Use the fixture as_of as the demo clock. If moving dates, shift the campaign fixture, observations, projections and lot dates together.

shopfloor_unavailable_response.reason: Company memory identifies a possible source, but shopfloor data is not yet available in this demo state.

plant.name: Skalvion accessory manufacturing
plant.scope: Accessory component conversion area, not the whole electronics factory

material_mapping.description: Pre-cut and edge-finished jeans fabric component for Smyle wristband

lines.name: Flexible accessory cell
lines.reason: Ready; no order scheduled this hour

shopfloor_timeseries_response.series_grain: one 15-minute interval per line; counts are interval deltas, not cumulative counters
shopfloor_timeseries_response.counter_scope: Final inspection output for a comparable accessory liner, followed by same-interval pack-out
shopfloor_timeseries_response.non_operating_hours: 16:00-08:00 omitted; all operating intervals, including idle and breaks, included

decision_summary.decision_scope: MAT000-7B material availability over the 14-day horizon; not finished-product delivery or all Q4 demand

capacity_basis.interpretation: Uncommitted NEW capacity; excludes existing work, existing inventory and observed historical output. Do not add operation capacities together.

decision_summary.decision_scope: MAT000-7B material availability over the 14-day horizon; not finished-product delivery or all Q4 demand

recovery_proposal_response.suggested_next_action: Approve the recovery schedule and release production/transfer orders through the Act 3 agent.
approvals_required: Isabella / supply-chain planning approval before any order release

monitoring_requirements.condition: expected Morvanto receipt misses material need date
monitoring_requirements.action: Escalate delivery risk and propose a revised plan

monitoring_requirements.condition: Updated yield or uncommitted input stock cannot support remaining lots

production_trend.note: Observed interval output on existing jobs; do not label as Smyle recovery output.

capacity_chart.note: Proposed production is a subset of available capacity, not another stacked supply source.

demand_coverage.note: Supply is at Morvanto after the one-day transfer, not simply output at Skalvion.

checks: Week 1 material identity, requirement, baseline supply and shortage match the existing campaign fixture.
456 intervals reconcile duration, runtime, stop and idle minutes; all observations are at or before the demo clock.
Good plus scrap equals total; OEE inputs reconcile and metric values stay within 0-100.
Operation WIP and adjacent-stage transfers reconcile; final pack-out matches line good output.
Daily proposals fit time-constrained bottleneck capacity and gross material requirements.
Transport-adjusted receipts cover every daily material need; no recovery lot is already released.
Weekly/daily/lot totals agree; no inventory, existing orders or historical output is counted as new capacity.
